speaker: margery_pell
text: You are in good time, Master Shakespeare, which from me is not a compliment. It means the stair is not yet a quarrel. The gallery is filling with coats.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Let it fill. I am not taking a count, and I am not taking a name to sew into this coat.

speaker: john_heminges
text: The bill is on the post. You may read it as you pass, or not. You are in the play. The book does not need you to announce yourself to the yard.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will read the title. I will not read myself into it. Paint is not on me yet. I would like that to stay true for a little.

speaker: margery_pell
text: Keep it true. A painted man on my stair before the doors is a man who wants to be looked at, and I have enough of those. The flag is up. The ground is cold. October does not owe you a warm yard.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not owed one. I will be inside until I am wanted, and I will come off when I am not.

speaker: john_heminges
text: That will do. The tireman is in his ordinary temper. It is not your cue.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then I will not make it my cue. Thank you, Margery. If the stair stays a stair, you will have had the better half of the afternoon.
